title: India Says Monsoon Crop Sowing Caught Up After July Rains

(Source: Bloomberg)

title: Copper's Upward Trend Can Continue, BlackRock Says
summary: "The trend is very much your friend," says Evy Hambro, head of fundamental equities thematic and sector investing at BlackRock, when asked about the rise in copper prices. "We are seeing a very tight market," he tells Bloomberg Television. "It's very easy to say: well, okay, it's gone up a lot and we should ignore it, and it's too late. The reality is, if you've done that you've missed out." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Libyan Protests Flare as Government Struggles to Keep Lights On
summary: Protests broke out again in the Libyan capital after the energy-rich country suffered its third widespread blackout in two days, fueling public anger over deteriorating basic services.

title: Bond Traders Are Hedging the Risk Fed Pivots to Cuts in 2027
summary: Bond traders are changing gears again. After a raft of data helped all but price out interest-rate hikes for the rest of the year, wagers in the options market are looking to hedge the risk that the Federal Reserve pivots to cutting rates in 2027.

title: Egypt Bond Risk at 2014 Low Shows Decade of Debt Distress Easing
summary: Record foreign-currency reserves and a vote of confidence from the International Monetary Fund have cut Egypt’s risk premium to the lowest since 2014.

title: Pakistan’s Record IPO Year Gets Boost From SE Fruits Listing
summary: Fresh produce company SE Fruits and Vegetable Ltd. is planning an initial public offering in Pakistan next month to boost its export capacity, adding to a record year of listings in the country.

title: Absa CEO: Africa Expansion Plan Progressing Well
summary: Absa Group is exploring the possibility of converting its representative office in Nigeria into a merchant bank. Chief Executive Officer Kenny Fihla also said he sees opportunities in Uganda, Zambia, Tanzania, Angola. He spoke to Bloomberg’s Chief Africa correspondent, Jennifer Zabasajja, to discuss their plans after the group reported net income for the first half-year of 12.58 billion rand vs. 11.23 billion rand y/y. (Source: Bloomberg)
